parts.title: Section 3
parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][312333]} {[Once upon a time, if a television show with any self-respect wanted to target a young audience, it needed to have an e-mail address.][312334]} {[However, in Europe’s TV shows, such addresses are gradually substituted by telephone numbers so that audiences can text the show from their mobile phones.][312356]} {[Therefore, it comes as no shock that according to Gartner’s research, texting has recently surpassed Internet usage across Europe.][312381]} {[Besides, among the many uses of text messaging, one of the fastest-growing uses is to interact with television.][312401]} {[The statistics provided by Gartner can display that 20% of French teenagers, 11% in Britain and 9% in Germany have responded to TV programmes by sending a text message.][312420]}

{[B.][312450]} {[This phenomenon can be largely attributed to the rapid growth of reality TV shows such as ‘Big Brother’, where viewers get to decide the result through voting.][312452]} {[ The majority of reality shows are now open to text-message voting, and in some shows like the latest series of Norway’s ‘Big Brother’, most votes are collected in this manner.][312480]} {[But TV-texting isn’t just about voting.][312511]} {[News shows encourage viewers to comment by texting messages; game shows enable the audience to be part of the competition; music shows answer requests by taking text messages; and broadcasters set up on-screen chatrooms.][312519]} {[TV audiences tend to sit on the sofa with their mobile phones right by their sides, and ‘it’s a supernatural way to interact.][312554]} {[’ says Adam Daum of Gartner.][312578]}

{[C. Mobile service providers charge appreciable rates for messages to certain numbers, which is why TV-texting can bring in a lot of cash.][312594]} {[Take the latest British series of ‘Big Brother’ as an example.][312616]} {[It brought about 5.][312627]} {[4m text-message votes and £1.][312635]} {[35m ($2,1m) of profit.][312641]} {[In Germany, MTV’s ‘Videoclash’ encourages the audience to vote for one of two rival videos, and induces up to 40,000 texts per hour, and each one of those texts costs €0.][312647]} {[30 ($0.][312681]} {[29), according to a consultancy based in Amsterdam.][312684]} {[The Belgian quiz show ‘1 Against 100’ had an eight-round texting match on the side, which brought in 110,000 participants in one month, and each of them paid €0.][312691]} {[50 for each question.][312722]} {[In Spain, a cryptic-crossword clue invites the audience to send their answers through text at the expense of €1, so that they can be enrolled in the poll to win a €300 prize.][312728]} {[Normally, 6,000 viewers would participate within one day.][312760]}

{[At the moment, TV-related text messaging takes up a considerable proportion of mobile service providers’ data revenues.][312770]} {[In July, Mm02 (a British operator) reported an unexpectedly satisfactory result, which could be attributed to the massive text waves created by ‘Big Brother’.][312788]} {[Providers usually own 40%-50% of the profits from each text, and the rest is divided among the broadcaster, the programme producer and the company which supplies the message-processing technology.][312812]} {[So far, revenues generated from text messages have been an indispensable part of the business model for various shows.][312842]} {[Obviously, there has been grumbling that the providers take too much of the share.][312861]} {[Endemol, the Netherlands-based production firm that is responsible for many reality TV, shows including ‘Big Brother’, has begun constructing its own database for mobile-phone users.][312876]} {[It plans to set up a direct billing system with the users and bypass the providers.][312902]}

{[D. How come the joining forces of television and text message turn out to be this successful?][312919]} {[One crucial aspect is the emergence of one-of-a-kind four-, five- or six-digit numbers known as ‘short codes’.][312936]} {[Every provider has control over its own short codes, but not until recently have they come to realize that it would make much more sense to work together to offer short codes compatible with all networks.][312953]} {[The emergence of this universal short code was a game-changer, because short codes are much easier to remember on the screen, according to Lars Becker of Flytxt, a mobile-marketing company.][312990]}

{[E. Operators’ co-operation on enlarging the market is by a larger trend, observes Katrina Bond of Analysys, a consultancy.][313033]} {[When challenged by the dilemma between holding on tight to their margins and permitting the emergence of a new medium, no provider has ever chosen the latter.][313051]} {[WAP, a technology for mobile-phone users to read cut-down web pages on their screens, failed because of service providers’ reluctance towards revenue sharing with content providers.][313078]} {[Now that they’ve learnt their lesson, they are altering the way of operating.][313104]} {[Orange, a French operator, has come such a long way as to launch a rate card for sharing revenue of text messages, a new level of transparency that used to be unimaginable.][313119]}

{[F. At a recent conference, Han Weegink of CMG, a company that offers the television market text-message infrastructure, pointed out that the television industry is changing in a subtle yet fundamental way.][313149]} {[Instead of the traditional one-way presentation, more and more TV shows are now getting viewers’ reactions involved.][313178]}

{[Certainly, engaging the audiences more has always been the promise of interactive TV.][313197]} {[An interactive TV was originally designed to work with exquisite set-top devices, which could be directly plugged into the TV.][313211]} {[However, as Mr Daum points out, that method was flawed in many ways.][313231]} {[Developing and testing software for multiple and incompatible types of set-top box could be costly, not to mention that the 40% (or lower) market penetration is below that of mobile phones (around 85%).][313245]} {[What’s more, it’s quicker to develop and set up apps for mobile phones.][313282]} {[‘You can approach the market quicker, and you don’t have to go through as many greedy middlemen,’ Mr Daum says.][313296]} {[Providers of set-top box technology are now adding texting functions to the design of their products.][313318]}

{[G. The triumph of TV-related texting reminds everyone in the business of how easily a fancy technology can all of a sudden be replaced by a less complicated, lower-tech method.][313336]} {[That being said, the old-fashioned approach to interactive TV is not necessarily over; at least it proves that strong demands for interactive services still exist.][313363]} {[It appears that the viewers would sincerely like to do more than simply staring at the TV screen.][313389]} {[After all, couch potatoes would love some thumb exercises.][313408]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 5:

Reading Passage 3 has seven sections, A-G. Choose the correct heading for sections B-G from the list of headings below.

Write the correct number, i-ix, inboxes 1-5 on your answer sheet.  

List of Headings

i           An application of short codes on the TV screen
ii          An overview of a fast-growing business
iii         The trend that profitable games are gaining more concerns
iv         Why Netherlands takes the leading role
v          A new perspective towards sharing the business opportunities
vi         Factors relevant to the rapid increase in interactive TV
vii        The revenue gains and bonus share
viii       The possibility of the complex technology replaced by the simpler ones
ix         The mind change of set-top box providers 

Example:    Answer

Section A    ii

questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "vi"

This phenomenon => đang trở tới việc "dùng text messaging để interact with television" ở đoạn trước

- This phenomenon phần lớn LÀ DO (be attributed to) sự phát triển của reality TV shows, khán giả có thể decide the result through voting
- Phần sau nêu thêm những chương trình khác thì audience có thể text để làm gì (news shows thì có thể comment || game shows thì có thể tham gia vào cuộc thi || musics shows thì đưa ra request các bài nhạc || ....)

=> đều là những yếu tố giải thích cho phenomenon - "dùng text messaging để interact with television" ở đoạn trước

Đáp án "vii"

 

- Câu đầu: TV-texting mang lại nhiều tiền bởi vì các nhà mạng charge phí khá cao khi nhắn cho những số nhất định (số của các chương tình chẳng hạn)

- Phần sau là ví dụ cụ thể về lợi nhuận ở các nước để làm rõ tại sao "TV-texting mang lại nhiều tiền"

- Đoạn sau: cái lợi nhuận (profit) đó được chia như thế nào giữa nhà mạng với nhà đài

Đáp án "i"

 

- sự thành công của texting television là nhớ và short codes (có thể là 4 kí tự hoặc 5 hoặc 6 kí tự)

- Phần sau giải thích rõ ra short code dùng để làm gì: mỗi nhà mạng có short code của riêng mình, nhưng gần đây thì họ nhận ra nên có short codes mà compatible với tất cả các mạng => dễ nhớ hơn

Đáp án "v"

 

- khi phân vân giữa "holding on tight to their margins (lợi nhuận)" và "sự xuất hiện của new medium" thì ko có ai chọn the latter (ko ai chọn a new medium" => nhà mạng nào cũng cũng ôm khư khư lợi nhuận về phần mình (và việc này có hại)

- câu sau: ví dụ WAP là minh chứng cho cái hại của việc "ôm khư khư lợi nhuận về phần mình" mà ko chia cho content providers

- Câu cuối: từ đó các nhà mạng rút ra bài học là cần phải chia lợi nhuận cho các bên. Ví dụ là nhà mạng Orange của Pháp

Đáp án "viii"

 

sự thành công của TV texting nhắc nhở những người trong ngành công nghiệp này về việc một công nghệ fancy (xịn) có thể bất ngờ bị thay thế bới công nghệ đỡ complicated hơn (việc  dùng apps để thay thế cho set-top box)

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 6 - 8:

Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.  

Write the correct letter in boxes 6-8 on your answer sheet.

questions.explanationHtml:
đáp án "A"

nghiên cứu cho thấy rằng việc nhắn tin đã vượt qua việc sử dụng Internet, mà một những mục đích của nhắn tin đang phát triển nhanh nhất là nhắn tin để tương tác với TV
Phần sau là ví dụ ở nhóm tuổi teenagers một số nước ở Europe

options.text: They would be part of the competition.
Their participation could change the result.

questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "D"

trong những reality TV shows, khán giả có thể quyết định kết quả thông qua việc bầu chọn

options.text: increasing their share in the market.
setting up a modified set-top box.

questions.explanationHtml:
Đáp án "C"

người ta đang chuyển từ chỉ nhắn tin thông qua set-top devices  (exquisite set-top devices) sang thông qua những app được xây cho điện thoại (nhanh hơn và rẻ hơn) -
building an embedded message platform
(platform - nền tảng ở đây là app)
